findings.where: Desktop first screen, the hero: the red 'write to me' margin note, the page's one call to action
findings.fault: When you squint at the first screen, the large headline, the clipped photo and the wide aqueduct sketch all outweigh the only call to action. It is a small red scrawl in the left margin. It doesn't line up with the headline, the lead line or the tagline: it floats just below the tagline's line, apart from everything it should be read with. Nothing guides the eye from 'Mark M. Moseley, infrastructure advisor' to it.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided they want to contact Mark. On the first screen the way to do that is the least noticeable thing, so they look to the nav's 'Contact' or leave. The homepage's job is to get them in touch.

findings.where: Article specimen, desktop: the two-line title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' and the handwritten pull quote
findings.fault: Each line snaps to every other ruled line, so the space between the two title lines is about as large as the space between the title and the byline. The title breaks into two separate-looking lines and stops reading as one heading (proximity). The pull quote has the same gappy leading. On the phone the same title is set tight, so the gap comes from the rule grid and isn't intended.
findings.who_objects: A reader opening one of Mark's articles. They expect a heading to read as one unit before the text. Angélique will publish every post in this template, so every long title will break apart this way.

findings.where: Article specimen, the PDF row 'Streamlining the PPP Process… | Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF', at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The row's closing rule runs right under the last line of text, touching the descenders and looking like an underline or strike. The opening rule has a clear gap above the text, so the row looks lopsided and cramped.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning for Mark's lecture PDF. The bottom rule reads as an underline on only part of the row, which blurs where the link starts and ends. Every PDF Angélique attaches will show the same collision.

findings.where: Palette tile: the colour chips and their name / hex / use captions, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each three-line caption sits as close to the chip in the next row as to its own chip above it. The captions are also spread one per ruled line, so a chip and its label don't hold together as a group (proximity).
findings.who_objects: Mark, or the layout round, reading the tile to pick colours. It takes a second look to be sure which name belongs to which chip.

findings.where: Phone, the motion sketch's timeline table
findings.fault: The four-column table is kept at 390 px. The Element column narrows to one or two words per line, so each row is a tall, ragged stack, about 12 lines for the 'Hold' row, beside three nearly empty columns. It is the busiest block on the phone page.
findings.who_objects: Mark, if he reviews the direction on his phone. The one table that explains the animation is the hardest thing on the page to read.
